name: Personal Expense Tracker
tagline: Record income and spending, set a monthly budget and see where your money goes in charts.
description: A React and TypeScript web app for tracking personal finances. Add income and expenses with categories, filter them by period, type, category and note, follow a monthly budget, and explore spending in a category donut chart and a six-month income-versus-spending bar chart. Amounts are stored as whole minor units to avoid rounding errors, and all data stays in the browser.
features: Add, edit and delete income and expense transactions with an amount, category, date and optional note.
Eight spending categories and five income categories, each with its own chart colour.
Filter by this month, last month, last 30 days, this year, all time or a custom date range, and by type, category and note text.
Income, spending and balance totals calculated from the filtered transactions.
Monthly budget with a progress bar showing the amount left or how far over budget you are.
Spending-by-category donut chart and a six-month income-versus-spending bar chart, each with a table view.
Export filtered transactions as CSV, and export or import a validated JSON backup.
Currency formatting for INR, USD, EUR, GBP and JPY, including Indian digit grouping.
Money stored as integer minor units and parsed without floating-point rounding.
limitations: Data is stored in one browser on one device; there is no sync or account.
There is no bank or UPI integration; every transaction is entered by hand.
Changing the currency does not convert amounts that were already saved.
Categories are fixed in the code; adding custom categories needs a small code change.
Recurring transactions such as monthly rent must be entered each time.
learningObjectives: Represent money safely with integers and format it with Intl.NumberFormat.
Derive totals and chart data from state with pure, testable functions.
Draw accessible charts with Recharts and provide table alternatives.
Validate imported JSON before trusting it.
Test React components and user flows with Vitest and Testing Library.
ideasForExtension: Support recurring transactions such as rent and subscriptions.
Let users create their own categories and store them with the data.
Add per-category budgets with alerts when a budget is close to running out.
Import transactions from a bank statement CSV file.

prerequisites.name: Node.js
prerequisites.note: Node.js 24 LTS is recommended. npm is included.

steps.title: Install the dependencies
steps.note: Needs an internet connection the first time and downloads about 180 MB into node_modules.

steps.title: Start the app
steps.note: Open the address Vite prints, usually http://localhost:5173/. Press Ctrl+C in the terminal to stop.

steps.title: Build for production (optional)
steps.note: Creates an optimised copy in the dist folder and serves it locally.

notes: Transactions are saved in your browser’s localStorage under the key campuskit-expenses:v1.
To reset data, use Budget & data in the app, or delete that localStorage entry from your browser’s developer tools.
Change the app name, currency, default budget, accent colour and demo data in src/app.config.json.

covers: Parsing and formatting money in several currencies without rounding errors.
Date ranges for every period filter, totals, category shares and monthly series.
Budget status, including going over budget.
Backup and localStorage validation with clear error messages.
Demo data scaling and CSV formula-injection protection.
User flows: adding and editing transactions, validation, chart table view, filtering and deleting.

network.notes: npm install downloads packages once. After that the app runs offline and never sends data anywhere.
